claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic or near-equiatomic.
Powder metallurgy can be used to synthesize HfNbTaTiZr from powders.
Relative elemental percentages can be altered by changing the proportions of elemental powders before consolidation.
Spark plasma sintering can consolidate HfNbTaTiZr powders.
The proposed samples should be processed under an inert atmosphere while sintering temperature, pressure, and other parameters are held constant.
Systematic variation of constituent percentages will produce measurable changes in the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
Compositional shifts in HfNbTaTiZr can change its grain size.
Compositional shifts in HfNbTaTiZr can change phase uniformity and induce secondary-phase formation.
Elemental composition alters solid-solution strengthening in HfNbTaTiZr.
Elemental composition alters phase stability in HfNbTaTiZr.
Changes in solid-solution strengthening and phase stability modify dislocation mobility.
Composition-dependent mechanisms can promote grain refinement or phase segregation.
Microstructural refinement is associated with increased hardness in processed HfNbTaTiZr.
Increasing the levels of strengthening elements may increase hardness relative to an equiatomic baseline.
Increasing the levels of strengthening elements may increase yield strength relative to an equiatomic baseline.
The relationship between composition and mechanical properties may be nonlinear.
The predicted strengthening behavior is bounded by the single-phase solid-solution stability region.
Excessive compositional deviation may cause phase separation or detrimental secondary phases.
A composition series can be evaluated using microscopy, Vickers hardness, and tensile or compressive strength tests.
The hypothesis is falsified if compositional variation produces no statistically significant microstructural or mechanical-property change relative to the equiatomic baseline.
